The work is done. The waiting is the hard part.

This isn't a theory we invented in a pitch deck. It's one of the most-discussed frustrations in freelancer and small-business communities — scored 18/20, the top pain point in our October 2026 research across US, UK, and EU forums.

“How do you deal with a client who takes FOREVER to pay?”
— Alignable small-business forum thread · 58,000 views · 6,300 comments (alignable.com, cited in research, Oct 19, 2026)
“I hate chasing invoices — it makes me feel like a debt collector.”
— Recurring phrasing on r/freelance (cited in research, Oct 19, 2026)
“Is there any tool that automatically reminds clients to pay?”
— Search & forum query pattern tracked across r/freelance and r/smallbusiness (research, Oct 19, 2026)
58kviews on one Alignable thread about late-paying clients
6.3kcomments on that same thread — this is not a niche gripe
1–3×per month: how often project-based earners hit this, per the research

The pattern in the research is consistent: people don't avoid chasing because they're disorganised. They avoid it because it feels awkward, they fear damaging the relationship, or they simply forget in the middle of real work. Accounting software buries reminders three menus deep. NudgePay is built around the one job those tools treat as an afterthought.

How NudgePay will work

Four steps, designed so the uncomfortable part — deciding what to say, and when — is handled for you, while the decision to send never is.

1

Add the invoice

Enter it by hand or import a CSV. Client, amount, due date — that's all NudgePay needs to start a chase.

2

We draft the ladder

A five-step sequence is prepared for you: −3 days, due date, +3, +7, and +14 days — each one a notch firmer than the last.

3

You approve, in one tap

Every draft waits for you. Read it, edit any line, approve or skip. Nothing sends on a timer behind your back.

4

Client pays in the message

Each reminder carries its own Pay Now link. When it's paid — via the link or marked by you — the sequence stops instantly.

Launch channel: email — where the paper trail lives. WhatsApp is the planned first addition after launch; join the waitlist and tell us if it's the channel you need most.

Built to protect the relationship, not just chase the money

Human approval, always

The feature everything else hangs on. Sequences prepare drafts; humans send them. It's the difference between a helpful nudge from you and an automated dunning machine with your name on it — and it's why clients stay clients after they pay.

Recovery dashboardIllustrative preview — not live data
Invoice #1042 · Bloom Studio · $2,400$2,400 recovered
Invoice #1038 · Northwind · $1,150Day +3 draft waiting
Recovery rate (example view)Shown per invoice, never hidden

The dashboard we are building shows amount outstanding, amount recovered, and recovery rate — so you can see, in pounds/dollars/euros actually received, whether the tool is earning its fee.

Pay Now in every message

Every reminder carries a payment link for that exact invoice. No “please see attached,” no bank details to copy, no friction to hide behind. Paid via the link? The sequence stops automatically.

Email + WhatsApp

Email for the paper trail at launch, WhatsApp for the clients who live there — planned as the first addition after launch, with the same ladder and the same approval step. Tell us on the waitlist if WhatsApp is the channel you need most; demand there decides how fast it ships.

Founding pricing — help us test it

We're validating pricing before we build billing. The anchor is real: indie tools in this space (PayRemind, at $5–25/mo) have shown freelancers will pay to remove the awkwardness. We're testing whether $9–19/mo is the right shape — pick the one you'd actually pay.

Straight answers

No launch theatre. Here's where things actually stand.

That's the risk the whole product is designed around. The ladder starts before the due date with a friendly heads-up, stays courteous through the due date and +3 days, and only gets firm at +7 and +14 — by which point most freelancers in our research said they wished they'd said something firmer sooner. You also see and can edit every word before it sends, and you can stop a sequence the moment a client replies or pays part of the invoice.

No. Approval is the core mechanic, not a setting. Drafts are prepared on schedule, but a message only leaves when you tap Approve for that specific message. If you ignore a draft, it expires — it does not send itself later.

Email is the launch channel. WhatsApp is the planned first addition after launch, because for many small businesses — especially outside the US — that's where clients actually respond. When it arrives it will use the same ladder and the same approval step. We are not planning phone calls or letters; if a client needs that level of escalation, that's a collections conversation, and NudgePay is deliberately not a debt-collection agency.

Honestly: not yet, and we won't invent a date. NudgePay is in Phase 0 validation right now — this page exists to test whether enough freelancers and small businesses want it. If the waitlist validates, the founding cohort gets access first, in small batches, so we can watch real invoices get recovered before opening up. Joining the waitlist is the fastest way to be in that first batch.

An invoice counts as recovered when the money actually arrives: either paid through the Pay Now link in a reminder, or marked as paid by you after a bank transfer or other payment. A client opening an email doesn't count. A promise to pay doesn't count. This definition matters most for the Pay-as-you-recover test plan — you'd only be charged on money in your account.

No, and no. NudgePay is intentionally not accounting software — it's the one layer accounting tools bury: the chase itself. You can add invoices by hand or CSV import without any accounting platform. Integrations, if waitlist members ask for them, would come after launch, not before.

Your next late payer doesn't have to become an awkward email you rewrite six times.
